# Facebook Posts Scraper

The Apify actor [`apify/facebook-posts-scraper`](https://apify.com/apify/facebook-posts-scraper) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its build **0.0.404**. The module's version is that build number, and every run it starts is pinned to exactly that build, so the input types below are the ones the actor really runs with.

Extract posts, videos, and engagement metrics from Facebook pages. Get text captions, reactions, video transcripts, images, external links, collaborators, and more from Facebook pages and profiles. Export ad data, schedule runs via API, and integrate with other tools or AI workflows.

## Pricing

Pay per event — Post $0.005, Actor start $0.001, Add-on: Date filter $0.002 (Free-plan prices; paid plans pay less). Cap the spend with `maxTotalChargeUsd`.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/apify/facebook-posts-scraper) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/apify-facebook-posts-scraper@0.0.404#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs:
      startUrls: []
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `startUrls` | array | yes |  | Facebook URLs — Enter a valid Facebook page URL, e.g. https://www.facebook.com/humansofnewyork/. Note that you can only scrape public pages with this Actor, not personal profiles. |
| `resultsLimit` | integer |  |  | Results amount — Set how many posts should be scraped per page. For example, if set to 5, the scraper will extract up to 5 posts from each page. This setting is ignored when scraping direct post URLs. If this limit is not set, as many results as possible are returned. |
| `captionText` | boolean |  | `false` | Include video transcript — Extract video transcript (if available). |
| `onlyPostsNewerThan` | string |  |  | Posts newer than — Scrape posts from the provided date to the present day (or date set in 'Older than'). The date should be in YYYY-MM-DD absolute format or in relative format, e.g., 1 day, 2 months, 3 years. The JSON input also supports adding time units (UTC timezone): Full or partial ISO timestam |
| `onlyPostsOlderThan` | string |  |  | Posts older than — Scrape posts from the provided date to the past (or date set in 'Newer than'). The date should be in YYYY-MM-DD or full ISO absolute format or in relative format e.g. 1 days, 2 months, 3 years. The JSON input also supports adding time units (UTC timezone): Full or partial ISO time |

## Output

Each dataset item is typed from the actor's published dataset schema. Every field may be null, and items may carry fields beyond these.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `facebookUrl` | string \| null | URL of the Facebook page or profile the post was scraped from. |
| `postId` | string \| null | Facebook post ID. |
| `url` | string \| null | URL of the Facebook post. |
| `time` | string \| null | Date and time the post was published, in ISO 8601 format. |
| `timestamp` | number \| null | Unix timestamp of when the post was published. |

| `collaborators` | array \| null | Collaborators tagged in the post. |

| `comments` | number \| null | Number of comments on the post. |
| `shares` | number \| null | Number of times the post was shared. |
| `topReactionsCount` | number \| null | Total count of top reactions on the post. |
| `reactionLikeCount` | number \| null | Number of Like reactions. |
| `reactionLoveCount` | number \| null | Number of Love reactions. |
| `reactionHahaCount` | number \| null | Number of Haha reactions. |
| `reactionWowCount` | number \| null | Number of Wow reactions. |

| `reactionAngryCount` | number \| null | Number of Angry reactions. |
| `reactionCareCount` | number \| null | Number of Care reactions. |
| `media` | array \| null | Media attachments (photos, videos) included in the post. |

| `previewSource` | string \| null | Source domain of the link preview. |
| `previewTarget` | object \| null | Target object of the link preview. |
| `isVideo` | boolean \| null | Whether the post contains a video attachment. |
| `viewsCount` | number \| null | Number of video views (for video posts). It is the number that matches the view count numbers you see on Facebook. This view is counted once the video has been watched for at least 1 second. |

| `sharedPost` | object \| null | The original post data if this post is a share. |

| `topComments` | array \| null | Top comments on the post. |
